stories.headline: We're being subjected to cognitive warfare by adversaries, need to bolster capabilities: CDS
stories.title: We're being subjected to cognitive warfare by adversaries, need to bolster capabilities: CDS
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 27: Chief of Defence Staff Gen N S Raja Subramani on Friday said the distinction between war and peace is "blurring" today and there is a "continuous state of contestation", cautioning that warfare in cyber, electronic and cognitive domains is already occurring. Delivering an address here on the 'Future of warfare and India's preparedness to conduct multi-domain operations', he also said, without elaborating, "We are being subjected to cognitive warfare by our adversaries in an insidious way" to weaken the will and morale of the nation, and emphasised bolstering capabilities in all domains. The general officer, during an interactive session after delivering his talk at a seminar, also asserted that "we are well-geared, along our northern frontier". Asked how he saw China successfully launching on Wednesday its Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship carrying three astronauts, including Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the CDS said Pakistan's space capability is "improving" with China's help, and positional navigation and other domain-related capabilities available with the Chinese will be available to the Pakistanis, so that will have to be "factored into our calculus". He also spoke on the significance of air power, and said that for bolstering the Navy's prowess, there is a need for more unmanned surface vessels, unmanned underwater vessels and enablers to increase their range. "We want to be joint in design, multi-domain in orientation, have a tech-enabled capability, be Aatmanirbhar in thought and action, and finally a capable human-centric leadership," the CDS said. Gen Anil Chauhan (retd), who was the CDS during Operation Sindoor last year, moderated the session hosted by think-tank Vivekananda International Foundation in Delhi. The CDS, in his address, outlined 10 major trends which, he said, are defining the future of warfare, underlining that the first is the expanding nature of the battlefield. "Secondly, the distinction between war and peace is increasingly (getting) blurred. We are in a state of continuous contestation. "Cyber, space, electronic warfare and cognitive warfare are already occurring, and that means they will precede a conflict, they will occur during the conflict, and they will outlast the conflict. So, we cannot say that we are either in a state of peace or war; we are in a continuous state of contestation," he said. The CDS said that in coordination with the three services, efforts are underway to "modernise our electronic warfare architecture". Elaborating his point on the idea of "continuous contestation" and the blurring of the distinction between peace and war, he said, "Even today, we are being subjected to cognitive warfare by our adversaries in an insidious manner, to sow (seeds of) division in society, create internal rifts, weaken the will and morale of the nation." "Therefore, it is important that we understand cognitive warfare and information warfare, and a commander today will have to spend as much time on operations as he has to devote time to information warfare," the CDS added. It is "not a supporting function", it is a "primary function of the commander". It is one of the important building blocks as far as multi-domain operations are concerned, he said. He cited multiple conflicts in the last few years, from the Azerbaijan-Armenia conflict to the Ukraine conflict and the US-Israel-Iran conflict. "Economically, wars in one part of the world can affect everybody... When we look at the Iran-Israel war, we see that closure of Strait of Hormuz in terms of critical minerals, fertilisers, energy is affecting each and everybody in the world, and led to loss of (US President Donald) Trump in the (US) mid-term elections. So, unintended effects," he said. "The other unintended effect as far as we are concerned is the Makkah alliance," the CDS said. Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Makkah on August 7. The pact establishes a framework for collective deterrence and stipulates that an armed attack against any one of the three countries would be regarded as an attack against all three. The CDS also cited Operation Sindoor, terming its second phase an excellent example of joint, integrated, multi-domain operations, and asserted that India not only had control over the escalation matrix and escalation dominance, but it also resulted in a "decisive victory" for India. Gen Raja Subramani underlined the evolving nature of technology and the warfare, however, cautioning that technological superiority is "only transitory" and this will need constant improvement to stay prepared for future wars. He emphasised that a whole-of-nation approach is needed to fight and sustain a prolonged war. The general officer said multiple-domain operations is not about combining all the capabilities, rather it implies integrating different capabilities to "pose multiple dilemma to an adversary". He said integration of military-space architecture and the ability to communicate effectively are key to carrying out such operations and cyber defence is an integral component of it, he added. The CDS further said an integrated command and control system is a prerequisite for conducting such operations. On military preparedness, at a time when multiple conflicts are underway, he said, "We need not look at a prescribed template. We need to have our own template."

stories.title: Tamil Nadu BJP chief welcomes Supreme Court order to light Deepam at Deepathoon
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu BJP chief welcomes Supreme Court order to light Deepam at Deepathoon
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: Tamil Nadu BJP chief Nainar Nagendran added that the Supreme Court could be approached again if the lamp was left unlit.
Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagendran on Friday welcomed the Supreme Court’s order to light the Karthigai Deepam lamp at the Deepathoon on Madurai’s Thiruparankundram hill on November 28.
Speaking to India Today, Nagendran said he expected the lamp to be lit on Saturday and indicated that the Supreme Court could be approached again if its order was not carried out.
Asked about his earlier remarks linking the row to Chief Minister Vijay’s Christian faith, Nagendran said Vijay was not personally responsible for lighting the lamp.
The dispute is over where on the hill the lamp should be lit.

The Tamil Nadu government says the traditional site is the mandapam near the Uchippillayar shrine, while petitioners have sought to light it at the Deepathoon, a stone pillar higher up the hill near a dargah.
The bench said the failure to light the lamp at the pillar on November 24 appeared to be wilful disobedience of its November 20 order.

It issued contempt notices to Tamil Nadu’s Chief Secretary, the Director General of Police and 13 others, asking them to appear on December 15 and explain why contempt proceedings should not be initiated against them.
The court suspended the board of trustees of the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple and appointed retired High Court judges Vaidyanathan and Parthiban to take over its administration.
It handed security of the hill to the Central Reserve.
Police Force and directed it to ensure that devotees could visit the dargah and perform their rituals.
The court directed the retired judges to consult temple functionaries and, if the flame at the Uchippillayar mandapam was still burning, use it to light the Deepam at the pillar.

stories.headline: RBI Guv to MSMEs: Take advantage of the lower tariffs available under India’s FTAs
stories.title: RBI Guv to MSMEs: Take advantage of the lower tariffs available under India’s FTAs
stories.summary: Malhotra observed that only about 20–30 per cent of eligible Indian exports take advantage of the lower tariffs available under India’s FTAs
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra on Friday exhorted MSMEs (micro, small and medium enterprises) to look beyond domestic markets and take advantage of the lower tariffs available under India’s FTAs (Free Trade Agreements).
In his address at the SME Finance & Investment Summit, Malhotra observed that only about 20–30 per cent of eligible Indian exports take advantage of the lower tariffs available under India’s FTAs.
This is remarkably low compared with 60–70 per cent utilisation by partner countries’ exports to India.
“It is an opportunity we are leaving on the table.
Learn about the FTAs relevant to your products, invest in quality, standards and certification, and draw on the support available from the agencies concerned,” he said.
The Governor highlighted the importance of formalising the financials of MSMEs and earning the confidence of their lenders.
“Every lasting business relationship rests on trust.
Customers stay with you because you deliver quality on time; suppliers stay with you because you keep your commitments.
Lenders are no different.
“You will obtain credit on better terms if you keep proper accounts, file returns on time, transact digitally and manage your finances with discipline.
Increasingly, the data trail your business leaves behind will count for as much as the assets you can pledge,” he said.
Malhotra encouraged the MSMEs to use the instruments built for them and treat support as a catalyst, not a crutch.

stories.headline: Supreme Court refuses to mandate unified portal for tracing unclaimed deposits; cites regulatory reforms
stories.title: Supreme Court refuses to mandate unified portal for tracing unclaimed deposits; cites regulatory reforms
stories.summary: Sucheta Dalal’s petition highlighted the accumulation of unclaimed deposits and investments with financial institutions and the procedural difficulties faced by nominees and legal heirs in recovering them
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 27, 2026) observed that regulatory reforms had substantially addressed the principal concerns raised in a plea seeking to facilitate the identification and recovery of unclaimed bank deposits, mutual fund investments and securities by legal heirs of deceased persons.
The court, however, declined to mandate the creation of a unified portal for tracing and reclaiming such assets, noting that substantial sector-specific mechanisms were already in place.
A Bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath and R. Mahadevan disposed of a public interest litigation (PIL) filed in 2022 by journalist and managing editor of Moneylife magazine Sucheta Dalal.
The PIL highlighted the accumulation of unclaimed deposits and investments with financial institutions and the procedural difficulties faced by nominees and legal heirs in recovering them.
“…we find that the principal concerns which prompted the institution of the present writ petition have been substantially addressed.

The subsequent establishment of centralised search facilities, simplification of claim procedures, strengthening of nomination and transmission mechanisms, and implementation of public awareness initiatives constitute significant progress towards addressing these concerns,” the Bench said, adding that any specific grievance concerning unclaimed financial assets may be pursued before the competent authority in accordance with law.

The petition sought directions to streamline the settlement of claims by legal heirs regarding bank deposits, insurance proceeds, post-office deposits and other financial assets to avoid unnecessary litigation.

It also stressed the need for a centralised online database under the aegis of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), providing particulars of deceased account holders, including their names, addresses and the dates of their last transactions.

The Bench noted that the RBI had launched the Unclaimed Deposits, Gateway to Access Information (UDGAM) portal in August 2023, enabling individuals to trace unclaimed deposits across multiple banks through a common platform.

The search facility was subsequently extended to 30 banks, which together accounted for approximately 90% of the unclaimed deposits held in the Depositor Education and Awareness Fund (DEAF) in terms of value.

The Department of Financial Services informed the court that unclaimed financial assets worth approximately ₹6,453 crore had been returned to their rightful claimants as of April 18, 2026, through a nationwide campaign titled ‘Aapki Poonji, Aapka Adhikar’, launched in October last year.
Outreach and facilitation camps had been organised across 748 districts.

stories.headline: Supreme Court grants bail to former AAP legislator Naresh Balyan
stories.title: Supreme Court grants bail to former AAP legislator Naresh Balyan
stories.summary: A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh passed the order while hearing Mr. Balyan’s plea challenging a Delhi High Court order denying him bail in the case
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 27, 2026) granted bail to former Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) legislator Naresh Balyan, who was booked under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) over his alleged association with U.K.-based gangster Kapil Sangwan.
A Bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh, while granting bail, directed Mr. Balyan to cooperate with the trial proceedings.
Mr. Balyan had approached the court after the Delhi High Court rejected his bail plea.
In August, the High Court had denied Mr. Balyan bail, observing that the registration of 17 FIRs against the alleged crime syndicate was indicative of “continuing unlawful activity” under the MCOCA.
Justice Manoj Jain had further held that prolonged incarceration could not be the sole consideration for granting bail in cases involving serious offences under stringent penal statutes.
During the hearing, senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for Mr. Balyan along with advocate Vivek Jain, submitted that key prosecution witnesses had retracted their statements.

He also pointed out that Mr. Balyan had himself lodged a complaint with the police alleging threats from the very gangster with whom he was accused of having links, following which he was provided police protection.
Opposing the bail plea, Additional Solicitor General Raja Thakare, appearing for the Delhi.
Police, submitted that the case involved serious allegations of organised crime, including land grabbing and extortion.

He argued that the applicability of the MCOCA did not hinge on the registration of multiple cases against an individual accused but on the criminal activities of the organised crime syndicate, against which, he said, 19 cases had been registered.
In his petition, Mr. Balyan pointed out that he had been in custody since December 2025 and that the investigation against him was complete.
He further contended that the evidence relied upon by the prosecution was inadmissible and that he had not initially been named in the case.

stories.headline: MP Choudhary Ramzan records 91% attendance in Rajya Sabha
stories.title: MP Choudhary Ramzan records 91% attendance in Rajya Sabha
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 27: National Conference (NC) Rajya Sabha MP Chowdry Mohammad Ramzan recorded 91 per cent attendance, participated in 21 debates and raised 32 questions during his first three parliamentary sessions, with issues concerning Jammu and Kashmir’s infrastructure, employment, agriculture and environmental security featuring prominently in his parliamentary interventions. According to parliamentary performance data compiled by PRS Legislative Research, Ramzan’s attendance stood 11 percentage points above the national average of 80 per cent and four percentage points above Jammu and Kashmir’s average of 87 per cent. Ramzan, who took oath on December 1, 2025, participated in the Winter Session of 2025, followed by the Budget and Monsoon sessions of 2026, covering 45 parliamentary sittings up to August 13, 2026. His parliamentary participation came despite disruptions during the Monsoon Session, which affected the conduct of parliamentary business. Among the key issues raised by the MP were the construction of the Sadhna and Razdan Pass tunnels, all-weather connectivity to isolated border regions, the proposed Sopore-Kupwara railway link, extension of the Baramulla railway line and the Bandipora-Lolab road project. Ramzan also sought details from the Centre on stalled bridge and tunnel projects in rural Jammu and Kashmir, road connectivity between Machil and Tangdhar via Keran, and the inclusion of Bungus Valley under the National Ropeways Development Programme. Employment and economic concerns featured prominently in his parliamentary questions, with the MP seeking details regarding a special employment package for Jammu and Kashmir, safeguards for horticultural crops in view of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and the promotion of high-density plantations. During parliamentary proceedings, Ramzan raised concerns over the threat to Kashmir’s horticulture industry from harmful agrochemicals and apple imports, besides flagging issues concerning hydroelectric power projects, particularly in the Chenab Valley. On environmental and public welfare issues, the MP sought information regarding Jammu and Kashmir’s vulnerability to Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs), the drinking water crisis, drug addiction surveys and seizures, and micro-irrigation facilities. His parliamentary interventions also covered school education infrastructure, telecom services, tourism promotion in Kupwara, the status and completion timeline of Government Medical College Handwara and the operationalisation of the Khelo India Excellence Centre at Gulmarg. Beyond region-specific matters, Ramzan participated in discussions on the Union Budget 2026–27, the Motion of Thanks on the President’s Address, the functioning of the Ministry of Rural Development and several legislative proposals. These included Bills concerning public examinations, the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, Central Armed Police Forces, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and the strength of Supreme Court judges. Through Special Mentions and other parliamentary interventions, Ramzan also raised the demand for granting classical language status to Kashmiri, the attack on former Chief Minister Farooq Abdullah, the need to uphold communal harmony and the safety and evacuation of Indian nationals from Gulf countries.

According to parliamentary performance data compiled by PRS Legislative Research, Ramzan’s attendance stood 11 percentage points above the national average of 80 per cent and four percentage points above Jammu and Kashmir’s average of 87 per cent.
body: Ramzan, who took oath on December 1, 2025, participated in the Winter Session of 2025, followed by the Budget and Monsoon sessions of 2026, covering 45 parliamentary sittings up to August 13, 2026.
His parliamentary participation came despite disruptions during the Monsoon Session, which affected the conduct of parliamentary business.

Among the key issues raised by the MP were the construction of the Sadhna and Razdan Pass tunnels, all-weather connectivity to isolated border regions, the proposed Sopore-Kupwara railway link, extension of the Baramulla railway line and the Bandipora-Lolab road project.

Ramzan also sought details from the Centre on stalled bridge and tunnel projects in rural Jammu and Kashmir, road connectivity between Machil and Tangdhar via Keran, and the inclusion of Bungus Valley under the National Ropeways Development Programme.

Employment and economic concerns featured prominently in his parliamentary questions, with the MP seeking details regarding a special employment package for Jammu and Kashmir, safeguards for horticultural crops in view of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and the promotion of high-density plantations.

During parliamentary proceedings, Ramzan raised concerns over the threat to Kashmir’s horticulture industry from harmful agrochemicals and apple imports, besides flagging issues concerning hydroelectric power projects, particularly in the Chenab Valley.

On environmental and public welfare issues, the MP sought information regarding Jammu and Kashmir’s vulnerability to Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs), the drinking water crisis, drug addiction surveys and seizures, and micro-irrigation facilities.

His parliamentary interventions also covered school education infrastructure, telecom services, tourism promotion in Kupwara, the status and completion timeline of Government Medical College Handwara and the operationalisation of the Khelo India Excellence Centre at Gulmarg.

Beyond region-specific matters, Ramzan participated in discussions on the Union Budget 2026–27, the Motion of Thanks on the President’s Address, the functioning of the Ministry of Rural Development and several legislative proposals.
These included Bills concerning public examinations, the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, Central Armed.
Police Forces, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and the strength of Supreme Court judges.

Through Special Mentions and other parliamentary interventions, Ramzan also raised the demand for granting classical language status to Kashmiri, the attack on former Chief Minister Farooq Abdullah, the need to uphold communal harmony and the safety and evacuation of Indian nationals from Gulf countries.

stories.headline: Rohit Sharma back as Mumbai Indians captain; five-time winner to lead team in IPL 2027
stories.title: Rohit Sharma back as Mumbai Indians captain; five-time winner to lead team in IPL 2027
stories.summary: Rohit Sharma will return as Mumbai Indians captain for IPL 2027 following Hardik Pandya's trade to Punjab Kings. The five-time IPL-winning skipper, who was replaced by Hardik ahead of the 2024 season, returns to the leadership role after three seasons. Rohit, who joined Mumbai Indians in 2011 and took over the captaincy in 2013, will lead the franchise in its 20th season of the IPL, chasing a sixth IPL title.
